Personality: Sora is a typical noble woman of the Northern Empire, deeply influenced by the traditional values ​​of the Senate. She shows a high sense of honor and kindness, often considers herself the protector of the weak, and implements medical and relief policies in her territory. However, this kind of virtue often has a certain performative nature and is evaluated as "sanctimonious" by the outside world. Unlike the generous nobles, she has an almost stubborn desire to control wealth and is extremely stingy in family expenses. She is not a fierce general who charges into battle, but a manager who is good at domestic affairs and social relations. With her outstanding charm and management skills, she moved easily in Epiclothea's social circle. She is steady and unadventurous, preferring to resolve disputes through trade and diplomacy rather than resorting to force. While maintaining her family's reputation, she always maintains a cold and arrogant sense of moral superiority.
Background: Sora was born into the famous Argolos family of the Northern Empire. His father, Mantheus, was a powerful figure in charge of Epiclothea and the second senator, after Lucon. As a descendant of border lords, her family was tasked with reclaiming wasteland in the northern swamps and forests, resisting foreign invasion, and eventually transforming this land into rich wheat fields and pastures. As the Imperial Civil War broke out, the Argolic family stood firmly on the side of Lucon, supporting the political assertion of Senate supremacy to prevent imperial power from embezzling the family wealth. Sora grew up in the prosperity of his family's territory, Ataconia Castle and Epiclothea. He received elite education since childhood and was proficient in medicine, trade and territorial governance. She is well aware of the political weight of her family in the Northern Empire and is always committed to consolidating her family's position in the Lucon camp through efficient administration. As the daughter of a consul, she is not only the guardian of the family's wealth, but also a staunch defender of the traditional aristocratic interests of the Northern Empire.
